observations.title: Kilauea volcano (United States)
observations.description: The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) reported that the eruption within Kilauea?s Kaluapele summit caldera, characterized by episodic fountaining, incandescence, and intermittent spatter from craters along the SW margin of Halema`uma`u Crater, continued at variable levels during 10-15 September. Occasional incandescence and flames were observed in webcams images from all three eruptive vents (S, W, and N) at Halema`uma`u Crater. On 10 September overflows were less frequent, slower, shorter in duration (less than 10 minutes), not fed by a dome fountain, and did not travel as far from the N vent. Overflows during the morning of 11 September were more vigorous and lasted longer than 10 minutes. Several of these were fed by dome fountains that were 5-10 m tall. They also traveled farther from the N vent compared to those from the 10th. There were 104 lava overflows from the N vent during 7-12 September, with the last one starting at 0727 on 12 September. Occasional spattering and flames were observed from the W vent and less frequently from the S vent; more energetic spatter and large flames were noted during drainback events. Each overflow during 11-12 September averaged about 20 minutes, separated by periods of about 10-15 minutes. The size and vigor of the dome fountains in the N vent gradually doubled in size to 10-15 m high on 12 September. Intermittent spatter bursts were visible at the N vent during the early morning of 13 September and increased in intensity throughout the day. Around noon, the bursts began depositing spatter that started to build a small cone on the rim of the N vent. During the afternoon, effusive activity began to cool within the upper regions of the conduit. There were distinct Strombolian eruptions reported throughout the night, characterized by large, individual spatter bursts. A seismic swarm consisting of shallow earthquakes occurred during 2115-2125 on 13 September. Eruptive activity significantly slowed at 0600 on 14 September; no lava flows were observed after 12 September. By the afternoon of 14 September, the small cone around the N vent measured 11-12 m tall. Just before 2100, cracks on and near the base of the NW wall of Halema`uma`u Crater erupted lava just N of the vent complex. This was the same area where the short seismic swarm occurred the previous day.
